newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian cabinet wants police chief sacked.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian cabinet wants police chief sacked.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet decided on Thursday to ask President Zhelyu Zhelev to sack the national police chief over his failure to prevent crime, the state news agency BTA said.

The crime rate has soared since the collapse of communist rule in 1989 as Bulgaria moves slowly towards a market economy. Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev last week blamed corruption and low motivation among ill-paid policemen.
The cabinet proposed replacing police chief Ivan Dimov with his deputy Hristo Marinski.
Zhelev said earlier this year the ruling Bulgarian Socialist Party was too closely linked to mafia groupings to combat organised crime effectively.

In a separate development, state radio said Bulgaria's military prosecutor had filed a suit against an unidentified state official for illegally bugging telephones at the offices of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF).

UDF leader Ivan Kostov accused the Interior Ministry on November 5 of bugging the telephone of president-elect Petar Stoyanov at UDF headquarters and the military said it had found enough evidence to support his complaint.
Dobrev told a news conference last Friday: "I will resign if it is proved that any of my officers has a part in the illegal actions, such as bugging the phones of the opposition leaders."
Under Bulgarian law, illegal telephone tapping is punishable by two years imprisonment.
